:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: If $\cos x =- \dfrac {1}{3},$ find the value of $2\cos( x + 4\pi)+3.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The period of $y = \cos x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n$ we have

$$
\cos{x} = \cos{(x+2n\pi)} .
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡x & =cos⁡(x+2\cdot 2\cdot \pi ) \\  & =cos⁡(x+4\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\cos{x} =- \dfrac {1}{3},$ then $\cos{(x+4\pi)} = - \dfrac {1}{3}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}2cos⁡(x+4\pi )+3 & =2(-\frac{1}{3})+3 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}+3 \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
